editSteps.purpose: Preserve character C and create normal/disguised outfit views
editSteps.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: two-view character design sheet refining alien C for Mayhem Meadows, a low-poly third-person cartoon driving game.
Input images: the supplied image is the edit target and identity reference. It contains three characters A, B and C. Select ONLY character C at the far right, the tall lanky blue-gray alien in a mustard human jacket. Do not include characters A or B in the output.
Primary request: preserve C's recognizable identity and lanky proportions, put him in a more neutral posture and expression, replace his human clothes with more alien clothing, and show a second variant of the same character wearing an obviously fake moustache, eyebrows and disguise.
Scene/backdrop: the same simple pale warm-gray studio backdrop and soft contact shadows.
Composition/framing: one wide sheet with two equal, generously separated full-body views of the SAME alien, both in the same relaxed three-quarter-front standing pose. Left: normal alien outfit. Right: identical character and alien outfit with added comically unconvincing disguise. Equal scale, head and feet fully visible, no overlap. No text or panel letters.
Identity invariants: keep C's blue-gray skin, broad flattened elongated bald head with extended cranium, pronounced central angular nose ridge, narrow chin and long neck, small dark eyes with pale sclera, long thin arms and legs, narrow shoulders and lanky adult build. Retain his specific head silhouette and facial geometry from the right-hand character. Not a classic grey, not the green mechanic, not a new character.
Posture/expression change: head upright and level, back comfortably upright, shoulders relaxed, arms resting naturally down at his sides with hands visible, feet comfortably spaced, balanced stance. Relaxed eyelids, level brow and gently closed straight mouth, attentive neutral expression. Remove the smirk, side-eye, stoop, cocked hip and hands-behind-back pose. He should seem calm and mildly curious without smiling.
Alien clothing change: replace the Earth-style bomber jacket, shirt, conventional trousers and lace-up shoes with a practical extraterrestrial outfit. A simple muted mustard-and-charcoal asymmetric wrap tunic with a high split collar, a diagonal overlapping front panel, an off-center broad geometric clasp, subtle large angular seam lines and short split hem; charcoal fitted leg coverings and narrow seamless gray ankle boots. Simple molded segmented forearm cuffs and a small flat geometric device at one hip. Clothes should read as alien through unusual construction rather than elaborate machinery. Preserve restrained colors and low-poly modelability, with large readable forms and few details. No Earth lapels, shirt buttons, tie, jeans, military armor or elaborate greebles.
Disguise variant on right: use exactly the same face, neutral expression, pose, body, skin and alien outfit as the left. Add an intentionally obvious cheap human disguise: thick rectangular black costume spectacles with clear lenses so the eyes remain visible, two very conspicuous crooked black stick-on eyebrows attached above the glasses, an oversized bushy black fake moustache visibly stuck under his long nose, and an undersized plain brown human trilby perched on top of his unusually wide alien head. The moustache and eyebrows should look like angular low-poly costume props with plainly visible light adhesive tabs at their outer edges. His alien skull, long neck and blue-gray skin remain completely exposed; disguise is comically unconvincing. Do not replace or cover his signature nose with a novelty nose. No face mask, no human skin, no real facial hair.
Style invariants: match the supplied character's flat-shaded faceted low-poly 3D game-concept rendering, matte surfaces, simple daylight-like studio lighting, subdued palette, broad geometry and dry humor. Retain adult proportions. Avoid cute mascot styling, giant sparkling eyes, chibi bodies, photorealism, horror, aggressive expressions, weapons, text, logos and watermark.

editSteps.purpose: Refine both faces to a neutral resting expression and forward gaze
editSteps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Input image: edit target, the two-view sheet showing the same lanky blue-gray alien in an asymmetric mustard-and-charcoal outfit, with an obvious taped moustache-and-eyebrow disguise in the right view.
Change only the facial expression and eye gaze of BOTH characters to a calm neutral resting expression. Remove the remaining upturned smile/smirk: draw a short straight relaxed horizontal closed mouth, no raised corners. Set both eyes looking straightforward in the direction the head faces, not sideways. Set the original facial brow ridges level and relaxed, with naturally open unexaggerated eyelids. On the right keep the crooked fake stick-on eyebrows as costume props; the underlying face is neutral.
Preserve everything else exactly: the specific alien's facial geometry and identity, head shapes, blue-gray skin, elongated nose and cranium, body proportions, relaxed upright arms-down posture, hand positions, all clothing, cuffs, boots and hip device, the entire right-hand disguise including hat, glasses, fake moustache, fake eyebrows and visible adhesive tabs, left/right arrangement, equal scale, full-body framing, backdrop, shadows, low-poly faceting, lighting and palette. No new objects, no text, no crop.
